say.text: A junior wrote TOF revision notes at 11 pm. Each note hides one planted mistake, and the mistakes are ones real PYQs are built on.
Your job: find the error, then fix it. Where the old key and the current source disagree, you get both.
Note 1: "Classic TOF = large VSD + overriding aorta + RVOT obstruction + ASD."
What is wrong with it?

choices.label: ASD is not one of the four; it replaced RVH
It should list LVH as the missing component
It should list PDA as the missing component

say.text: Count the real four: a large VSD, an overriding aorta, RVOT obstruction and a ventricular hypertrophy. Which item in the note is not on that list?

Found it. Classic TOF is a **large, anteriorly malaligned VSD**, an **overriding aorta**, **infundibular RVOT obstruction** and **right ventricular hypertrophy**. ASD may accompany TOF but is not one of the four.
PYQs have keyed PDA, ASD and LVH as "not part of TOF", and current StatPearls agrees with the four above.
Tempting: the note has no hypertrophy at all, so a ventricular item does look missing.
But the missing fourth component is **right** ventricular hypertrophy, never LVH. The planted error is the ASD sitting in its place; PYQs key LVH as "not part of TOF".

sure_note.text: You were sure, so lock in the side: the hypertrophy of TOF is right ventricular.

say.text: Tempting: a PDA may accompany TOF, so it feels like a natural fifth item.
But accompanying is not being one of the four. The four listed by StatPearls and CDC include no ASD, PDA or LVH, and PYQs key them as "not part of TOF".

sure_note.text: You were sure, so remember: PDA and ASD may accompany TOF, yet neither is a component.

say.text: Note 2: "Pentalogy of Fallot = TOF plus a PDA."
Fix the note.

choices.label: It is TOF plus an atrial septal defect
The note is right: PDA is the fifth lesion

say.text: Think back to Note 1: the lesion that wrongly sat among the four is the one that completes the pentalogy.
**Pentalogy of Fallot** = TOF plus an **atrial septal defect**; the term is old and seldom used now.
PYQs have expected pentalogy of Fallot = TOF + ASD, and CDC confirms it.
Tempting: PDA is the other lesion that, like ASD, may accompany TOF.
But the pentalogy adds specifically an **atrial septal defect**, which PYQs expect and CDC confirms.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so fix it now: pentalogy means TOF + ASD, not PDA.

say.text: Note 3: "A boot-shaped heart on chest X-ray means the heart is enlarged."
Is the note right?

choices.label: No: the boot is an upturned apex from RVH

say.text: The boot describes the shape of the apex, and a hypertrophied right ventricle is what shapes it. Does the sign say anything about the heart simply being big?
Chest radiographs may classically show a **boot-shaped** heart, with an upturned apex due to right ventricular hypertrophy.
So the sign names a shape that RVH gives the heart, not a big heart.

choices.label: Do all infants show the boot?

say.text: Tempting: a hypertrophied ventricle sounds like a bigger heart.
But the sign is a shape, an upturned apex due to right ventricular hypertrophy, on a chest radiograph that may classically show the **boot**.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so re-read it: boot-shaped describes an upturned apex from RVH, not cardiomegaly.

say.text: Most infants with TOF, however, may not show the boot-shaped finding.
PYQs have keyed the boot-shaped heart to TOF; Radiopaedia says most infants with TOF may not show this finding.
Note 4: "The boot-shaped heart on chest X-ray confirms TOF. It is the investigation of choice."
Which fix is right?

choices.label: ECG is the gold standard instead
The note is right: the boot is diagnostic

say.text: A classic sign is not the same as the gold standard. Which investigation is the primary diagnostic modality?
Yes. The **echocardiogram** is the gold standard for diagnosis and remains the primary diagnostic modality.
The boot is a classic X-ray picture, not the confirming test.
Tempting: the boot is the classic chest X-ray picture, so it feels like the signature test.
But the **echocardiogram** is the gold standard and the primary diagnostic modality.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so file this: classic sign on X-ray, gold standard is echo.

say.text: Note 5: "TOF is the most common cyanotic CHD, and it most commonly presents in older children."
Which half is the error?

choices.label: The presentation: it most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate
Both halves are right; PYQs say beyond the neonatal period

say.text: The first half is a high-yield table entry. Only the second half is doubtful. At what age does TOF most commonly present?
TOF is the **most common cyanotic congenital heart disease**, and it most commonly presents as a **cyanotic neonate**.
Want the PYQ twist, or the numbers that differ between sources?
Tempting: the note echoes the old 'beyond the neonatal period' wording that some PYQs use. The deeper branch has that story.
But current StatPearls says TOF most commonly presents as a **cyanotic neonate**, so the presentation half is the error.
PYQs have expected TOF as the most common cyanotic CHD beyond the neonatal period, as Garagiola and Thorne state; current StatPearls says TOF most commonly presents as a cyanotic neonate.
The table entry reads: most common cyanotic CHD beyond the neonatal period, Tetralogy of Fallot.
For the exam, know both: the old key, and what the current source says.
Sources differ on frequency: 5 to 7 per 10,000 live births in StatPearls, 3-5 per 10,000 in Garagiola and Thorne, and about 3 to 6 per 10,000 in Gagliardi et al.
A **right aortic arch** is seen in 20-25% of TOF.
The 22q11.2 deletion is the most common syndromic association of TOF.
Last one, from a different angle. The junior asks you which of these IS a component of classic TOF.
Yes. The **overriding aorta** sits with the large VSD, infundibular RVOT obstruction and right ventricular hypertrophy.
ASD is tempting: it makes the old pentalogy and may accompany TOF.
But it is not one of the four; PYQs key ASD as "not part of TOF".

sure_note.text: You were sure, so this one is worth a second look: ASD is pentalogy, not a component.

say.text: PDA is tempting because it may accompany TOF.
But the four components listed by StatPearls and CDC include no PDA, and PYQs key PDA as "not part of TOF".

sure_note.text: You were sure, so re-check: may accompany does not mean component.

say.text: LVH is tempting because hypertrophy is on the list. The side is the trap.
The hypertrophy in TOF is **right** ventricular, and PYQs key LVH as "not part of TOF".

sure_note.text: You were sure, so check the side again: the fourth component is right ventricular hypertrophy.

say.text: Four components, pentalogy adds an ASD, echo is the gold standard, TOF is the most common cyanotic CHD and most often presents as a cyanotic neonate.
